title: Palindrome Check
prompt: Write `is_palindrome(s)` that returns True if `s` reads the same backward as forward (case-insensitive).

title: Reverse a String
prompt: Write `reverse_string(s)` that returns the string reversed, WITHOUT using slicing tricks like `s[::-1]` or `.reverse()`.

title: Vowel Counter
prompt: Write `count_vowels(s)` that returns the number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u — case-insensitive) in `s`.

title: Consonant Counter
prompt: Write `count_consonants(s)` that returns the number of consonant letters in `s` (ignore digits/spaces/punctuation).

title: Word Counter
prompt: Write `count_words(s)` that returns the number of words in a sentence (words are separated by whitespace).

title: Title Case Formatter
prompt: Write `title_case(s)` that capitalizes the first letter of every word and lowercases the rest.

title: Character Frequency
prompt: Write `char_frequency(s, target)` that counts how many times character `target` appears in `s`.

title: Anagram Detector
prompt: Write `is_anagram(a, b)` that returns True if `a` and `b` are anagrams of each other (same letters, same counts, ignore spaces/case).

title: Remove Vowels
prompt: Write `remove_vowels(s)` that returns `s` with all vowels (a, e, i, o, u, both cases) removed.

title: Space Stripper
prompt: Write `strip_spaces(s)` that removes all spaces from `s`, WITHOUT using `.replace(' ', '')`.

title: First Unique Character
prompt: Write `first_unique_char(s)` that returns the first character that doesn't repeat in `s`, or `None` if every character repeats.

title: String Compressor
prompt: Write `compress_string(s)` that turns `'aabcccccaaa'` into `'a2b1c5a3'` (run-length style compression).

title: Sub-string Search
prompt: Write `contains_substring(s, sub)` that checks whether `sub` occurs inside `s`, WITHOUT using the `in` operator.

title: Word Reverser
prompt: Write `reverse_words_order_kept(s)` that reverses each individual word's letters but keeps the word order the same. E.g. `'hi there'` -> `'ih ereht'`.

title: Pangram Check
prompt: Write `is_pangram(s)` that returns True if `s` contains every letter of the alphabet at least once.

args: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
Pack my box with five dozen liquor jugs

title: ASCII Sum
prompt: Write `ascii_sum(s)` that returns the sum of the ASCII values of every character in `s`.

title: Digit Extractor
prompt: Write `extract_digits(s)` that returns a string containing only the numeric characters found in `s`.

title: Alternating Case
prompt: Write `alternating_case(s)` that converts `s` to `AlTeRnAtInG` case, starting with an uppercase letter at index 0.

title: Longest Word Finder
prompt: Write `longest_word(s)` that returns the longest word in a sentence. If there's a tie, return the first one found.

title: Rot13 Cipher
prompt: Write `rot13(s)` that shifts every letter forward by 13 positions in the alphabet (wrapping around), leaving non-letters unchanged.

title: Even or Odd
prompt: Write `is_even(n)` that returns True if `n` is even, without converting to a string.

title: FizzBuzz
prompt: Write `fizzbuzz(n)` that returns a LIST of strings for 1..n: multiples of 3 -> 'Fizz', 5 -> 'Buzz', both -> 'FizzBuzz', otherwise the number as a string.

title: Prime Checker
prompt: Write `is_prime(n)` that returns True if `n` (an integer > 1) is prime.

title: Factorial (Loop)
prompt: Write `factorial(n)` that computes n! using an iterative loop (no recursion).

title: Fibonacci Sequence
prompt: Write `fibonacci(n)` that returns a list containing the first `n` Fibonacci numbers, starting with 0, 1.

title: Sum of Digits
prompt: Write `digit_sum(n)` that returns the sum of all digits in integer `n`.

title: Reverse an Integer
prompt: Write `reverse_integer(n)` that reverses the digits of integer `n` (e.g. 123 -> 321). Preserve the sign for negative numbers.

title: Leap Year Validator
prompt: Write `is_leap_year(year)` that returns True if `year` is a leap year (divisible by 4, except century years unless divisible by 400).

title: Armstrong Number
prompt: Write `is_armstrong(n)` that checks if `n` equals the sum of its own digits each raised to the power of the digit count (e.g. 153 = 1^3+5^3+3^3).

title: GCD / HCF
prompt: Write `gcd(a, b)` that returns the Greatest Common Divisor of two positive integers.

title: LCM
prompt: Write `lcm(a, b)` that returns the Least Common Multiple of two positive integers.

title: Number to Binary
prompt: Write `to_binary(n)` that converts a non-negative decimal integer to its binary string representation, WITHOUT using `bin()`.

title: Binary to Decimal
prompt: Write `to_decimal(b)` that converts a binary string `b` to its decimal integer value, WITHOUT using `int(b, 2)`.

title: Perfect Number
prompt: Write `is_perfect(n)` that returns True if the sum of `n`'s proper divisors (excluding itself) equals `n`.

title: Power Calculator
prompt: Write `power(a, b)` that computes a^b (b is a non-negative integer) WITHOUT using `**` or `pow()`.

title: Multiplication Table
prompt: Write `multiplication_table(n)` that returns a list of the products of `n` times 1 through 10.

title: Collatz Sequence
prompt: Write `collatz_steps(n)` that returns the list of values in the Collatz sequence starting at `n` until it reaches 1 (n/2 if even, 3n+1 if odd).

title: Square Root Approximation
prompt: Write `sqrt_floor(n)` that estimates floor(sqrt(n)) for a non-negative integer `n`, using only loops/integer math (no `**0.5` or `math.sqrt`).

title: Number of Divisors
prompt: Write `count_divisors(n)` that returns how many positive integers evenly divide `n`.

title: Strong Number
prompt: Write `is_strong(n)` that returns True if the sum of the factorials of `n`'s digits equals `n` (e.g. 145 = 1! + 4! + 5!).

title: Find Maximum
prompt: Write `find_max(arr)` that returns the largest value in a non-empty list, WITHOUT using `max()`.

title: Find Minimum
prompt: Write `find_min(arr)` that returns the smallest value in a non-empty list, WITHOUT using `min()`.

title: Second Largest
prompt: Write `second_largest(arr)` that returns the second highest distinct value in an unsorted list.

title: List Inversion
prompt: Write `invert_list(arr)` that returns a new list with elements reversed, WITHOUT using `.reverse()` or `[::-1]`.

title: Deduplicate List
prompt: Write `dedupe(arr)` that removes duplicate entries while keeping the original order of first appearance.

title: Linear Search
prompt: Write `linear_search(arr, target)` that returns the index of `target` in `arr`, or -1 if not found.

title: Binary Search
prompt: Write `binary_search(arr, target)` that finds `target`'s index in a SORTED list `arr` using binary search, or returns -1.

title: Count Occurrences
prompt: Write `count_occurrences(arr)` that returns a dict mapping each item in `arr` to how many times it appears.

title: Check Sorted
prompt: Write `is_sorted_asc(arr)` that returns True if `arr` is STRICTLY sorted in ascending order.

title: Merge Sequences
prompt: Write `merge_sorted(a, b)` that merges two already-sorted lists into a single sorted list.

title: Rotate Array
prompt: Write `rotate_left(arr, k)` that shifts list elements left by `k` positions (wrapping around).

title: Cumulative Sum
prompt: Write `cumulative_sum(arr)` that returns a list of running totals across `arr`.

title: Find Missing Number
prompt: Write `find_missing(arr, n)` that finds the single missing integer from a list that should contain 1..n exactly once each (minus one missing value).

title: Common Elements
prompt: Write `common_elements(a, b)` that returns a list of values present in BOTH `a` and `b` (no duplicates, order from `a`).

title: List Difference
prompt: Write `list_difference(a, b)` that returns items present in list `a` but not in list `b`.

title: Chunk Array
prompt: Write `chunk_array(arr, n)` that splits `arr` into a list of sub-lists, each of length `n` (the last chunk may be shorter).

title: Flatten List
prompt: Write `flatten(matrix)` that converts a 2D list into a single flat 1D list.

title: Move Zeroes
prompt: Write `move_zeroes(arr)` that moves all zeroes to the end of the list while keeping the relative order of non-zero elements.

title: Pair Target Sum
prompt: Write `pair_sum(arr, target)` that returns a sorted 2-element list `[a, b]` from `arr` where `a + b == target`, or `None` if no pair exists.

title: Check Subsequence
prompt: Write `is_subsequence(a, b)` that returns True if all elements of `a` appear in `b` IN ORDER (not necessarily contiguous).

title: Word Frequency Map
prompt: Write `word_frequency(s)` that returns a dict counting occurrences of each word (lowercased) in sentence `s`.

args: the cat sat on the mat

title: Invert Dictionary
prompt: Write `invert_dict(d)` that swaps keys and values in dictionary `d`.

title: Merge Dictionaries
prompt: Write `merge_sum(a, b)` that combines two dicts, SUMMING values for keys that appear in both.

title: Max Value Key
prompt: Write `max_value_key(d)` that returns the key with the largest value in dict `d`.

title: Dictionary Filter
prompt: Write `filter_above(d, k)` that returns a new dict keeping only entries whose value is greater than `k`.

title: Group by Length
prompt: Write `group_by_length(words)` that groups a list of words into a dict keyed by word length.

title: Phonebook Lookup
prompt: Write `phonebook_lookup(book, name)` that returns the phone number for `name` in dict `book`, or `'Not found'` if absent.

title: Nested Dict Extractor
prompt: Write `safe_nested_get(d, keys)` that walks a list of `keys` through nested dicts `d`, returning `None` if any key is missing along the way (no exceptions).

title: Character Counter Map
prompt: Write `char_count_map(s)` that returns a dict of character counts for string `s`.

title: Sort Dict by Keys
prompt: Write `sort_by_keys(d)` that returns a new dict with items sorted alphabetically by key.

title: Sort Dict by Values
prompt: Write `sort_by_values(d)` that returns a new dict with items sorted numerically by value (ascending).

title: Common Dict Keys
prompt: Write `common_keys(a, b)` that returns a SORTED list of keys present in both dict `a` and dict `b`.

title: Default Value Setter
prompt: Write `with_default(d, key, default)` that returns `d[key]` if it exists, otherwise `default` (no exceptions).

title: Frequency Threshold Filter
prompt: Write `filter_by_min_count(d, n)` that returns entries from count-dict `d` whose value is at least `n`.

title: Student Grade Classifier
prompt: Write `classify_grades(scores)` mapping each student name to a letter grade: A(>=90) B(>=80) C(>=70) D(>=60) F(below).

title: Roster Splitter
prompt: Write `split_pass_fail(scores, passing=60)` that groups student names into `{'pass': [...], 'fail': [...]}` based on `passing` threshold.

title: Shopping Cart Total
prompt: Write `cart_total(prices, cart)` that computes total cost, where `prices` maps item->price and `cart` maps item->quantity.

title: Count Unique Values
prompt: Write `count_unique_values(d)` that returns how many distinct values exist in dict `d`.

title: Key Renamer
prompt: Write `rename_key(d, old, new)` that renames key `old` to `new`, keeping its value (returns a new dict).

title: Dictionary Difference
prompt: Write `dict_diff(a, b)` that returns a SORTED list of keys whose values differ between dict `a` and dict `b` (including keys missing from one side).

title: Right Triangle Pattern
prompt: Write `right_triangle(n)` that returns a list of `n` strings forming a right-angled triangle of `*` (row i has i stars).

title: Pyramid Pattern
prompt: Write `pyramid(n)` that returns a list of `n` strings forming a centered pyramid of `*` (use leading spaces to center).

title: Inverted Triangle Pattern
prompt: Write `inverted_triangle(n)` that returns a list of `n` strings forming an upside-down triangle of `*`.

title: Diamond Pattern
prompt: Write `diamond(n)` that returns a list of strings forming a symmetric diamond of `*` with `n` rows in the top half.

title: Number Pyramid
prompt: Write `number_pyramid(n)` that returns a list of `n` strings; row i contains numbers 1..i separated by single spaces.

title: Pascal's Triangle
prompt: Write `pascals_triangle(n)` that returns a list of `n` lists, each being one row of Pascal's Triangle.

title: Matrix Addition
prompt: Write `matrix_add(a, b)` that returns the element-wise sum of two same-shaped 2D matrices.

title: Matrix Transpose
prompt: Write `transpose(matrix)` that swaps rows and columns of a 2D matrix.

title: Identity Matrix Checker
prompt: Write `is_identity(matrix)` that returns True if the square matrix is an identity matrix (1s on diagonal, 0s elsewhere).

title: Symmetric Matrix Checker
prompt: Write `is_symmetric(matrix)` that returns True if the square matrix equals its own transpose.

title: Flatten & Sort Matrix
prompt: Write `flatten_and_sort(matrix)` that unrolls a 2D list into 1D and returns it sorted ascending.

title: Spiral Matrix Order
prompt: Write `spiral_order(matrix)` that returns the elements of a 2D matrix visited in clockwise spiral order, as a flat list.

title: Diagonal Sum
prompt: Write `diagonal_sum(matrix)` that returns the sum of the main diagonal elements of a square matrix.

title: Tic-Tac-Toe Win Check
prompt: Write `check_winner(board)` for a 3x3 list of lists using `'X'`, `'O'`, or `''` for empty. Return `'X'` or `'O'` if that player has a winning row/column/diagonal, otherwise `None`.

title: Valid Sudoku Sub-Grid
prompt: Write `valid_subgrid(grid)` that checks if a 3x3 grid of ints contains each digit 1-9 exactly once.

title: Run-Length Encoding (RLE)
prompt: Write `run_length_encode(s)` that encodes repeating runs as `count+char` pairs, e.g. `'aaabb'` -> `'3a2b'`.

title: Run-Length Decoding
prompt: Write `run_length_decode(s)` that expands a run-length string like `'3a2b'` back into `'aaabb'`.

title: Roman to Integer
prompt: Write `roman_to_int(s)` that converts a Roman numeral string into an integer.

title: Integer to Roman
prompt: Write `int_to_roman(n)` that converts an integer (1-3999) into its Roman numeral string.

title: Balanced Parentheses
prompt: Write `is_balanced(s)` that checks if all brackets `()`, `{}`, `[]` in `s` are correctly matched and nested.

title: Recursive Factorial
prompt: Write `factorial_recursive(n)` that computes n! using RECURSION (the function calling itself).

title: Recursive Fibonacci
prompt: Write `fib_recursive(n)` that returns the n-th Fibonacci number (0-indexed: fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1) using RECURSION.

title: Recursive List Sum
prompt: Write `sum_list_recursive(arr)` that returns the sum of all numbers in `arr` using RECURSION, not a loop or `sum()`.

title: Recursive Power
prompt: Write `power_recursive(a, b)` that computes a^b (b >= 0) using RECURSION, without `**` or `pow()`.

title: Recursive Sorted Check
prompt: Write `is_sorted_recursive(arr)` that checks if `arr` is sorted ascending (non-strict), using RECURSION.

title: Tower of Hanoi Move Count
prompt: Write `hanoi_moves(n)` that returns the minimum number of moves needed to solve Tower of Hanoi with `n` disks.

title: Bubble Sort
prompt: Write `bubble_sort(arr)` that sorts a list ascending using the bubble sort algorithm, WITHOUT using `sorted()` or `.sort()`.

title: Selection Sort
prompt: Write `selection_sort(arr)` that sorts a list ascending using the selection sort algorithm, WITHOUT `sorted()` or `.sort()`.

title: Recursive Count Occurrences
prompt: Write `count_occurrences_recursive(arr, target)` that counts how many times `target` appears in `arr`, using RECURSION.

title: Recursive GCD
prompt: Write `gcd_recursive(a, b)` that computes the GCD of two positive integers using RECURSION (Euclid's algorithm).
